dragon-supreme: Tired of picking between a fast blade and a long one?

Random diamonds mean some work and some just ride along. The Dragon Supreme uses Zenesis diamond alignment, so the diamonds sit in a pattern and each one does its share. You get speed and life out of the same blade.
Segments taking a beating in heavy rebar?
Steel hammers a segment and heat works on the weld. The Dragon Supreme carries a 15mm double laser-welded segment, built to stay put through heavy rebar and hard highway concrete.
Swapping blades every time the material changes?

Most blades are bonded for one thing. This is the top of our line, built multi-purpose for cured concrete, asphalt, block, hard brick and pipe, so the blade stays on the saw and the crew stays cutting.
One blade for the cut-off saw and the walk-behind?
A core that is not tensioned for speed gets loose on a bigger saw. The Dragon line is speed tensioned, so the same blade can move from a cut-off saw to a low-horsepower walk-behind.
dragon: Blade worn out before the job is?
A bond that lets go of its diamonds too early burns through blades. The Dragon is a supreme combo blade bonded for life first. It is the one crews stretch the longest.
Core wearing thin under the segments in asphalt?

Abrasive slurry eats the steel right below the segment. That is undercutting. The Dragon has deeper drop segments that push slurry out of the cut and protect the core, so you wear out diamond, not steel.
Blade running hot and starting to wander?
Dust packed in the cut is friction, and friction is heat. The Dragon's deep keyhole gullets sweep debris out and cooling holes in the core move air, so it runs cooler and tracks straighter.
Concrete, then asphalt, then block, all before lunch?
A blade bonded for one material fights you in the next. The Dragon's combination segment is built to go from concrete to asphalt to block to pipe on the same saw, cut dry.
superblade-extreme: Saw beating up your hands by quitting time?
When every segment hits the same way, the blade sets up a chatter. The Superblade Extreme alternates its segment design to break that up, so you get less vibration and a quicker, smoother cut.
Ever had a blade warp or wobble?
When steel gets hot it gets soft and bends. The cooling holes in the Superblade Extreme move air through the whole blade so it runs cooler, which cuts the chance of warping and wobbling way down.
Asphalt chewing the core out from under you?
Soft, abrasive material grinds the steel below the segments. The drop segments on the Extreme sit deeper to protect the core, so the blade lasts until the diamond is used up.
Cutting more cured concrete than green?
Then this is your pick over the Super G. The turbo segments bite hard in cured concrete, pipe and stone. On mostly green slabs they run on the aggressive side, so go Super G there.
super-g: Four blades on the truck for four materials?
Most bonds are made for one material. The Super G is our best-selling multi-purpose blade, built for concrete, block, pavers, asphalt and pipe, so one blade stays on the saw through the whole day.
Losing blades to undercutting in asphalt?
Abrasive slurry wears the core under the segments until they let go early. On the Super G every fifth segment sits deeper to clear that slurry, so you wear out the diamond and not the core.
Cutting more green concrete than cured?
Aggressive turbo segments can be rough on a green slab. The Super G is the one we point to when green outweighs cured, and it still handles old cured concrete and rebar.

Dragging a hose slows a crew down. The Super G is built to cut dry, so you pull the cord and go. In the larger diameters it is meant for lower-horsepower saws, so ask us if you are not sure of the match.
t-rex: Blade riding the cut instead of biting?
A flat segment drags and builds friction. The T-Rex has a W-shaped crown segment that takes a heavy bite with less rubbing, so you get a quick, aggressive cut on concrete, rebar, brick and block.
Hot steel loses its tension and starts to wobble. The T-Rex runs an engineered cobalt steel core that is speed tensioned, built to resist heat warp and stay flat in the cut.
Need a solid blade for every saw in the yard?
Not every saw needs the top shelf. The T-Rex is our value blade with 10mm laser-welded segments, and it has been a go-to for concrete crews and masons for close to two decades.
viper-general-purpose: Leaning on the saw to make it cut?
A blade that loads up with dust stops hitting fresh material. The Viper's segmented turbo rim clears the cut and pulls itself through, so you push less and cut faster.
Pavers, block and curb on the same day?
Small jobs change material all day. The Viper is a basic general-purpose turbo blade for pavers, block, curb and patch work. It is not the top of our line, but it gets the job done.
Want a spare on every truck?
Jobs pop up and blades walk off. The Viper is a value blade in 12 and 14 inch with a 1 inch arbor, a sensible spare to hang on each cut-off saw.
superblade-g3: Blowing out edges on flagstone and granite?
A blade that grabs will chip the edge on natural stone. The G3's turbo segments give you control in the cut, which is why finish masons like it on flagstone, granite and bluestone.
Blade fast on Monday and slow by Friday?
A bond that does not wear right buries its diamonds. The G3 pairs an aggressive segment with a long-life bond, designed to keep cutting deep into the life of the blade.
Block, pavers and stone on one job?
Hardscape work changes material by the hour. The G3 is tuned for block, pavers, granite and natural stone, so the blade stays on and the crew keeps setting. It sits one step under the Dragon.
superblade-arrow: Blade glazing over on river rock or fire brick?
Hard, dense material polishes the diamonds flat and the blade quits cutting. The Arrow's bond is made for hard material and is built to stay open on rebar, river rock, fire brick and granite curb.
Burning through blades on hard material?
Hard rock uses up diamond in a hurry. The Arrow carries a 15mm segment, and a taller segment is more diamond to burn. Bigger segments typically mean longer blade life.
Slurry packing up in the cut?

When material builds up in the cut, all it does is slow the blade down. The arrow-shaped turbo segments throw it out so the blade keeps hitting fresh material, and they help guard against undercut wear.
Long hard cuts cooking your blade?
Dense material builds heat, and heat is what warps a core. The Arrow has a cooling-hole core and is speed tensioned, designed to run flat on a cut-off saw or a walk-behind.
zenesis-green-kut-purple: Hard rock in the mix slowing your joints down?

Hard aggregate dulls a blade that is bonded for softer stone, and then it rides instead of cutting. Purple is the Zenesis bond matched to hard aggregate, so it keeps cutting while the slab is still in the green zone.
Blade life all over the map from one blade to the next?

When diamonds are mixed in at random, some bunch up and some spots run thin. Zenesis sets the diamonds in a pattern, so each one works and the blade wears evenly. That is where the added footage comes from.
Chipped joints the GC makes you fix?
A blade that drags will ravel the edge of a fresh slab. The Zenesis Green Kut is designed for chip-free early-entry cuts, run dry, so the joint is clean the first time.
Not sure it fits your early-entry saw?
Early-entry saws use their own arbor patterns. Zenesis Green Kut comes in the arbor patterns for the common early-entry saws and in several thicknesses. Check both when you order.
arix-green-kut-purple: Cutting slabs poured with hard aggregate?
Hard stone wears on diamonds fast, and the wrong bond quits cutting clean. Purple is the Arix bond matched to hard aggregate, so the blade stays sharp in the rock you are sawing.
Why does one blade cut faster than the next?

Randomly mixed diamonds leave gaps and clumps in the segment. Arix arranges the diamonds in a pattern, so every one is lined up and working. The crew gets faster, more precise cuts and a clean finish.
Joint specs change from job to job. Arix Purple is stocked from 6 to 14 inch, with a quarter inch width in some sizes. Not every width comes in every diameter, so check the size list.
green-kut-purple: Blade quits cutting when the rock gets hard?
Each Green Kut color is a bond matched to how hard the aggregate is. Purple is made for hard aggregate. Match the color to your rock and the blade keeps cutting instead of riding on top.
Joints raveling when you cut the same day?
Fresh concrete tears if the blade drags. Green Kut is an early-entry bond made to cut joints the same day, so you get the control joint in before the slab cracks on its own.
Water and slurry on a fresh slab?
Nobody wants a hose on a finished floor. Green Kut blades run dry on an early-entry saw. Put a good skid plate on with the blade to help hold the joint edge.
punisher: Bit glazing up in heavily reinforced concrete?
Shotcrete and bridge deck are hard, dense and full of steel, and most bits polish over and quit. The Punisher's W-shaped segment is built for very heavily reinforced concrete and keeps cutting.
Bit running hot and packing with slurry?
A segment that stays dry runs hot and loads up. The dimples in the Punisher segment, like a golf ball, carry more water to the cutting face and clear slurry faster. Run it wet.
Coming up short means stopping to break out the core. The Punisher is stocked in 15, 18 and 24 inch barrels with 1-1/4 inch thread, so you can pick the depth the hole needs.
wolv: River rock or high-PSI concrete slowing the bit down?
Hard aggregate dulls ordinary diamond in a hurry. The Wolv uses patterned 35/45 mesh diamond in a cobalt and tungsten bond, built to hold up in reinforced concrete, river rock and hard aggregate.
Bit fast at the top of the hole and slow at the bottom?
Diamonds mixed in at random leave thin spots in the segment. The Wolv's diamonds are placed in a pattern, so each one is working from the first inch of the hole to the last.
Running a truck full of different bit lines?
Mixed brands means mixed threads and guesswork. The Wolv runs from small holes up to large diameters in three barrel lengths on 1-1/4 inch thread, so one line can cover most of the coring truck.
sabertooth: Bit overheating halfway down the hole?
When water gets flung off the segment, friction and heat take over. The Sabertooth's dimpled segments hold water in the cut longer, which reduces friction and helps the bit run cooler.

Most bits are bonded for one kind of rock. The Sabertooth segment was developed to perform across aggregates and job types, with heavy tungsten and cobalt content. It is the highest quality core bit we sell.
Customer asks for whatever your top bit is?
Then this is the one. It is stocked in 15, 18 and 24 inch barrels with 1-1/4 inch thread. Tell us the hole size, the depth and the material and we will match the barrel.
viper-premium: Blade polishing over on hard brick?
Hard brick and stone dull the diamonds, and a hard bond hangs onto them too long. The Viper Premium uses a soft bond that lets fresh diamond come through, so it keeps cutting clean and fast.
Abrasive material grinds a short segment down in no time. The Viper Premium has a 15mm segment height, so there is more diamond to work through. That is where the life comes from.
A blade that hammers the material leaves a ragged edge. The turbo-segmented rim on the Viper Premium cuts fast and leaves a clean edge. A solid value blade for masons, 14 and 16 inch.
blue-tornado: Diamonds falling out before they are used up?

When the bond lets go early, the diamond leaves before it has done its work. The Blue Tornado uses titanium-encapsulated diamond, designed to hold in the segment longer for a fast cut and longer life.
Blade heating up on long dry cuts?
Heat builds in the core on a long pass and the blade starts to move. The Blue Tornado's blue heat-sink core sheds heat fast, which helps the blade stay flat.
Dust packing in the cut and a screaming saw?
Dust that stays in the cut is drag and noise. The curved gullets on the Blue Tornado clear dust and help it run quieter, and the turbo segments leave a smooth finish.
Different blade line for every saw?
It is easier when the crew knows one blade. The Blue Tornado runs from 4 inch grinder sizes through 14 inch cut-off sizes. Check the arbor for your saw when you order.
blacksmyth: Abrasive wheel half the size by lunch?
An abrasive wheel grinds itself away, so your depth of cut shrinks all day. The Blacksmyth is vacuum-brazed diamond on a steel core. It holds its diameter, so the last cut is as deep as the first.
Worried about an abrasive wheel coming apart?
Abrasive wheels wear thin and can break apart under side load. The Blacksmyth is diamond brazed to a solid steel core, built to hold together, and it throws far fewer sparks and no wheel dust.
Hauling boxes of wheels to every job?
Wheels get used up fast on rebar, angle iron and pipe. One Blacksmyth lasts far longer than an abrasive wheel and cuts steel, rebar, angle iron, cast and ductile iron. Sizes run from 4 to 16 inch.
swordfish: Ordinary blade glazing over on hard, dense material?
Fire brick, engineered block and field granite polish a standard blade smooth. The Swordfish ripple turbo segment bites fast and keeps clearing the cut, so it keeps hitting fresh material.
Saw bogging in a deep cut?
Packed dust drags on the blade and loads the engine. The Swordfish has side-slit segments and extra-deep gullets to clear the cut, so it runs cooler and is less likely to bind.

A core that flexes under load walks off the line. The Swordfish runs a rigid, high-tensile core designed to track straight through heavy plunge cuts. Light, steady pressure lets the diamonds do the work.
jaguar: Segmented blade leaving a rough edge?
Gaps between segments hammer the material as they come around. The Jaguar has a continuous turbo rim, so it cuts quicker than a plain rim and leaves a cleaner edge on concrete, masonry and stone.
Grinder blades gone in a day?
A short rim does not have much diamond in it. The Jaguar carries a 10mm turbo rim, which gives it solid life for a grinder blade. It is our most popular premium turbo.
Which arbor does my grinder take?
Small saws are not all the same. The Jaguar runs from 4 to 10 inch, most with a 7/8 to 5/8 arbor and some with a diamond knockout. Match the diameter and arbor to your grinder or circular saw.
wolverine-premium: Core wearing out before the segments in asphalt?
Asphalt is soft but abrasive, and the slurry grinds the steel under the segments. The Wolverine Premium has slanted drop segments that shield the core from undercut wear.
Blade gone in a day of patching?

The wrong bond in asphalt wears away like chalk. The Wolverine Premium is bonded for asphalt and expansion joints, with a higher grade of diamond than the standard Wolverine, so it lasts in abrasive material.
Arbors differ between saws. The Wolverine Premium comes in 12 to 20 inch, with 1 inch and 20mm arbors in the common cut-off sizes. Check your arbor before you order.
turbo-cup-premium: Grinder leaving swirl marks you have to go back over?
Fewer segments dig harder and leave a rougher floor. More segments means a smoother finish. The Turbo Cup has fan-blade segments packed around the wheel for fast removal with a finer scratch.
Cup wheel getting too hot to keep grinding?
Grinding is all friction, and heat wears the wheel. The Turbo Cup Premium has double the cooling holes in the core to keep the wheel cool, which helps it last.
Grinders mount cup wheels two ways. This one comes threaded 5/8-11 or with a 5/8 to 7/8 arbor hole, in 4, 4.5 and 7 inch. Check your grinder spindle and the segment count you want.
blue-cheetah: Tuck pointing eating up the day?
A slow blade means more time on the scaffold. The Blue Cheetah has a high segment count built for aggressive, fast mortar removal, so the crew gets more joint cleaned per shift.
Blade cooking in a deep mortar joint?
A tight joint traps dust and heat around the blade. The Blue Cheetah's wide U-gullets clear the dust and its cooling holes help it run cool. It can be used dry or wet.
It runs on angle grinders, circular saws and tuck pointers. Sizes are 4 to 7 inch at a quarter inch wide with a 7/8 to 5/8 arbor. Match the width to your joint.
v-shape-wet-corebit: Bit skating around when you start the hole?
A flat segment wants to walk before it seats. The V-shaped segments on this bit come to a point, so it starts clean and gets cutting sooner.
Fewer diamonds in the segment means fewer holes. These V-Shape bits carry a higher diamond count with premium grade diamond for longer life. They are wet bits, so run them with water.
Thread changes with bit size. Over 2 inch diameter these are 1-1/4 inch 7 thread. Under 2 inch they are 5/8-11. Shank length is 14 inches and segments are laser welded.
hybrid: A hard bond holds dull diamonds too long on hard material, and the blade polishes over. The Hybrid uses a medium-soft bond that keeps fresh diamond coming, so it stays sharp on hard brick and stone.
Fast blade that does not last?
Soft-bond blades cut quick but can wear fast. The Hybrid is a supreme quality blade designed to give a fast, clean cut on most masonry without giving up blade life.
A rough-cutting blade ruins pieces you already paid to haul. The Hybrid's multi-segment design leaves clean edges on pavers and block, so there is less rework. It comes in 14 inch.
tornado: Grinder blade dragging in the cut?
Friction is what slows a small blade down. The Tornado's spiral T-segments move air through the cut to lower friction, so it feeds faster on concrete, brick, block and stone.
Blade chattering on a deep pass?
A thin core deflects when you lean into it. The Tornado has a reinforced steel core designed to cut down on chatter and flex on deeper passes.
Abrasive material pulls diamond out of a weak bond. The Tornado uses a cobalt bond to hold the grit, which is where its long life comes from. Sizes run 4 to 7 inch for grinders and circular saws.
double-row: Horseshoe marks all over the slab?
A single row cup wheel digs hard and leaves horseshoe marks. The Double Row is less aggressive and more forgiving, so it does not leave those marks behind.
One row of segments takes all the wear. Two rows of diamond share the work, so the Double Row lasts much longer than a single row.
Wheel overheating on a long grind?
Heat builds quick under a cup wheel. Cooling holes in the Double Row help keep it from overheating. It comes in 4, 4.5 and 7 inch, threaded 5/8-11 or with a 7/8 to 5/8 hole.
segmented-dry-corebit: Need a hole and there is no water?
Setting up water for a couple of holes eats time. These segmented bits are made for dry coring in concrete, brick, block and pavers with a hand-held core drill.
Worried about segments when coring dry?
Dry coring runs hot, and heat is hard on a weak weld. Every one of these dry bits is laser welded, built to hold its segments at dry-coring temperatures.
Will it thread onto my drill?
All of these dry bits are 5/8-11 thread with a 9 inch shank, sized for hand-held core drills. Diameters run from 1 to 6 inch.
25th-anniversary-blade: Segment height is how much diamond you have to burn. The 25th Anniversary Blade carries 15mm segments, so there is extra height and extra days on the saw.
One blade for cured concrete, asphalt and stone?
A single-purpose bond struggles when the material changes. This is a supreme combo blade engineered for life and speed across cured concrete, asphalt, block, brick and pipe.
A blade that chatters is hard on hands and arms. The Anniversary blade has a low-vibration core, which is easier on the operator late in a long shift. It comes in 14 inch with a 1 inch or 20mm arbor.
eagle-heavy-duty: General purpose blade wearing down too fast?
A short segment runs out of diamond early. The Eagle Heavy Duty has a 14mm sintered segment, so there is more height to wear through on cured concrete and masonry.
A loose core wanders in the cut. The Eagle Heavy Duty has a tensioned steel core that resists flex and helps it track straight.
Where does it sit in the line?
This is a good quality basic blade, not our top shelf. It comes in 12 and 14 inch with 1 inch or 20mm arbors, for crews that want a plain concrete blade that goes the distance.
eagle-premium: Not every cut calls for a supreme blade. The Eagle Premium is a basic blade for cured concrete and masonry that balances life and speed. Nothing fancy, nothing to babysit.
Cutting dry on a high-speed saw?
Dry cutting puts heat into the segment welds. The Eagle Premium has laser-welded segments, made for dry cutting on cut-off saws.
Need the same blade in a bigger size?
Crews often run more than one saw size. The Eagle Premium runs from 12 to 20 inch, so the cut-off saws and the small walk-behind can run the same blade.
eagle-premium-masonry: Need a 20 inch blade for the block saw?
Block saws and small walk-behinds need a bigger blade than a cut-off saw. This is the Eagle Premium in a 20 inch masonry bond for block, brick and concrete.
Is it the right bond for block?
Block and brick are abrasive, and a concrete bond can wear fast in them. This blade is bonded for masonry. It is a basic blade, plain and dependable.
What should I check before ordering?
It is one size: 20 inch with a 1 inch arbor. Confirm your saw takes a 20 inch blade and a 1 inch arbor, and whether you cut wet or dry on that saw.
eagle-standard: Just need a basic blade for a short job?
Some jobs do not call for a premium blade. The Eagle Standard is an economy segmented blade for concrete, brick and block. Plain and simple.
Is this the blade for daily production?
Straight answer: no. It is a basic economy blade. If the saw runs all day, step up to the T-Rex or a Superblade and you will change blades less often.
What sizes does it come in?
The Eagle Standard is a 14 inch blade with a 1 inch or 20mm arbor for cut-off saws. Check which arbor your saw takes.
eagle-supreme: Hard rock dulls a general-purpose bond. The Eagle Supreme is bonded for hard concrete and rebar, so the segments wear evenly and the blade keeps cutting.
Uneven pressure across the segment makes a blade grab. The Eagle Supreme has patterned segments that spread the pressure for a smoother cut with less chatter.
Where does it sit in the line?
It is the top of the Eagle line, built for long life on cured concrete and masonry. For mixed materials, the Super G and Superblade Extreme are the step up. It comes in 14 and 16 inch.
eagle-supreme-masonry: Cutting retaining wall block all day?
Wall block and CMU are abrasive and wear a concrete blade fast. The Eagle Supreme Masonry is designed for retaining wall block, concrete block, concrete pavers and CMU.
Need a 20 inch blade for the block saw?
Block saws take a bigger blade than a cut-off saw. This one is a 20 inch blade for table saws and walk-behinds.
What should I check before ordering?
Confirm your saw takes a 20 inch blade and check the arbor size. Tell us whether you run it wet or dry on that saw.
turbo-economy: This is our economy turbo for concrete and masonry on a cut-off saw. It is a basic blade for light use, described plainly.
Is it right for daily cutting?
Not really. An economy blade is for the occasional cut. If the saw runs every day, a Viper or T-Rex will hold up longer.
What sizes does it come in?
It comes in 12 and 14 inch at a standard .125 width. Check your saw's arbor size against the listing before you order.
viper-specialty: Hardest brick on the job killing blades?
Very hard brick and stone polish an ordinary bond. The Viper Specialty is specially bonded for the hardest materials, with a high diamond concentration for longer life.
A blade that hammers the edge chips it. The slanted segments on the Viper Specialty are designed for a fast cut with less chipping.
What sizes does it come in?
Two sizes: 14 inch for cut-off saws and 20 inch with a 1 inch arbor for bigger saws. Check your saw before you order.
viper-supreme-turbo: Hard pavers slowing your crew down?
Dense brick and stone resist a wide segment. The Viper Supreme Turbo has 48 split segments, designed to cut quick and smooth on the hardest masonry.
Pulling the blade out of the cut to let it cool?
On dense material a blade heats up, and stopping to cool it burns labor. The oversized cooling holes on this Viper help it shed heat so you can keep cutting.
Hands buzzing after a day of cuts?
A rough-running blade wears on the operator. The split-segment design runs with low vibration. It comes in 14 inch with a 1 inch or 20mm arbor.
wolverine-premium-plus-drop-segment: Green concrete chipping along the joint?
Wide gaps between segments slap a green slab and chip the edge. This Wolverine has tighter spacing between segments, which reduces chipping and speeds up the cut.
Green slab wearing the core out?
Green concrete is abrasive, and the slurry grinds the steel under the segments. The drop segments on this blade sit deeper to guard the core against undercutting.
Joints have a window, and a slow blade misses it. This blade is made for green concrete and feeds fast, so the joints get in on time. It comes in 14 and 16 inch.
wolverine-supreme: Asphalt wears the steel core under the segments. The fix on the Wolverine is a deeper drop segment that knocks slurry out of the cut before it eats the core.
Want speed and life in asphalt?
Usually a fast asphalt blade wears quick. The Wolverine Supreme is the top of the Wolverine line, designed to give both life and speed on asphalt and green concrete.
Blade heating up on long road cuts?
Long cuts build heat, and heat warps a core. The Wolverine line uses a cobalt steel core with U-gullets to fight heat warp. Sizes run from 12 to 20 inch with a 1 inch arbor.
eagle-small-diameter: Need a plain grinder blade for concrete?
This is our most popular premium segmented blade for grinders. It is a basic blade for cured concrete and masonry.
Small blades do not carry much diamond. The Eagle has 10mm segments, which gives it decent life for a basic blade. The segmented rim cuts dry.
It runs from 4 to 10 inch, most with a 7/8 to 5/8 arbor and a diamond knockout on the larger sizes. Match the diameter and arbor to your grinder or saw.
eagle-green-concrete: Cutting joints in fresh concrete with a small saw?
Fresh concrete is abrasive and wears a standard blade fast. The Eagle Green Concrete blade is engineered for cutting expansion joints in fresh concrete.
It comes with a universal arbor: 5/8 to 7/8 with a pinhole and a diamond knockout. That covers most grinders and circular saws.
What sizes does it come in?
Three sizes: 7, 8 and 10 inch. It is a basic Eagle blade, so pick the diameter for the depth of joint you need.
eagle-supreme-small-diameter: Stepping up from the basic grinder blade?
The Eagle Supreme small diameter uses a higher grade of diamond than the premium Eagle, so it lasts noticeably longer on brick, masonry and cured concrete.
Dry cutting needs airflow at the rim. The segmented rim on this blade lets air in, so it cuts fast and stays cooler.
It runs from 4 through 10 inch, so the common grinder sizes are covered. Check the arbor on your tool before you order.
granite-turbo: Cutting granite with a general purpose blade?
Granite is hard and a general bond tends to glaze on it. The Granite Turbo has a turbo rim bonded for granite and hard stone.
Why a turbo rim on stone?
A turbo rim cuts faster than a plain continuous rim and leaves a cleaner edge than a wide-gap segmented blade. That is a good fit for stone work.
What sizes does it come in?
Two sizes: 5 and 7 inch, for grinders and circular saws. Check your tool's arbor against the listing.
t-seg-turbo-black: Grinder blade choking on dense stone?
A plain turbo rim can load up and overheat on dense material. The T-shaped segment gives you a turbo edge for speed and a real segmented rim for airflow.
Blade polishing smooth on hard block?
Dense stone dulls a blade until it just rubs. The T-Seg design moves air and clears dust, which helps it keep cutting on brick, block and stone.
What sizes does it come in?
Three sizes: 4.5, 5 and 7 inch, for grinders and circular saws. Match the diameter to your tool and its guard.
dry-tile-blade: A segmented blade hammers tile and chips the glaze. This is a continuous rim blade, which gives a smoother edge on ceramic, marble and granite.
No tile saw on the job?
Hauling tile back to a wet saw wastes steps. This blade runs dry on a grinder, so you can make the cut where the tile sits.
The standard grade is for ceramic. The premium grade covers ceramic, marble and granite. Sizes run 4 to 7 inch, so check the arbor for your grinder.
dry-tile-supreme: Porcelain chipping with a regular tile blade?
Porcelain is harder than ceramic and shows every chip. The Dry Tile Supreme is a supreme-grade continuous rim blade made for porcelain.
This blade is made to run dry on a grinder, so you can trim tile at the install instead of walking it to a saw.
What sizes does it come in?
Three sizes: 4, 4.5 and 5 inch at a thin .060 width. Check the arbor on your grinder before you order.
j-slot-granite-blade: Granite heating up the blade on the table saw?
Granite is hard, and a solid rim can run hot in it. The J-slots in this rim help it cut faster and cooler.
It is a 10 inch blade for table saws. Confirm your saw's arbor and whether you run it wet before you order.
This one is bonded for granite. For porcelain, look at the Razor Porcelain or Turbo Superblade instead.
razor-porcelain-blade: Porcelain is hard and brittle, and a thick rim chips it. The Razor has a razor-thin rim designed for a clean edge on porcelain, so fewer tiles end up in the scrap pile.
Hard tile wears a lower grade of diamond quickly. The Razor uses supreme-grade diamond to stay sharp in the hardest tile.
Both. The Razor comes in 4, 7 and 10 inch, so it covers the grinder and the tile saw. Match the size and arbor to your tool.
turbo-superblade: Need speed in granite or porcelain?
A plain rim is clean but slow in hard material. The Turbo Superblade has a turbo rim that cuts fast and still leaves a clean edge.
Which one is for which material?
They are listed by material. The 4 inch is the granite blade and the 10 inch is the porcelain blade. Order the one that matches what you cut.
The 4 inch runs on a grinder and the 10 inch on a tile or table saw. Check the arbor on your tool before ordering.
wet-tile-blade: Tile saw blade chipping the glaze?
The wrong bond for the tile will chip it. These wet blades are listed by material: porcelain blades, and blades for ceramic, marble and granite.
No, these are wet tile saw blades. Run them with water on the saw. For dry cuts on a grinder, see the Dry Tile blades.
Sizes run from 6 to 14 inch. The 12 and 14 inch have a 1 inch arbor for larger saws. Match the diameter and arbor to your tile saw.
crack-chaser: Filler popping back out of a crack?
Filler does not hold in a ragged, dirty crack. The Crack Chaser's V-shaped segment opens the crack to a clean, uniform channel that is ready for filler.
Chasing with a regular blade means pass after pass. This blade has brazed, diamond-embedded wedges made for fast cutting and long life. It can be used dry or wet.
It comes in 4 and 7 inch, with a 7/8 to 5/8 arbor or 5/8-11 threaded. It runs on angle grinders, circular saws and tuck pointers. Check your spindle.
economy-tuck-point: This is the economy tuck pointer in our line. It is a basic blade for the short job, nothing more and nothing less.
Should I use it for a whole building?
Probably not. For daily mortar removal, a Sandwich or Blue Cheetah will last longer and cut quicker.
What sizes does it come in?
It comes in 4, 4.5 and 5 inch at a quarter inch wide for angle grinders. Match the width to your mortar joint.
premium-tuck-point: A general blade is not shaped for a joint. This is a premium tuck point designed for efficient mortar removal.
Not every joint is a quarter inch. This one is the .187 thick tuck point, for tighter joints, in 4, 4.5 and 5 inch.
What should I check before ordering?
Measure the joint and match the blade thickness to it. Then match the diameter and arbor to your grinder.
sandwich-tuck-point: Tuck point blade dragging in the joint?
A solid wide rim rubs both sides of the joint. The Sandwich design joins two segmented blades into one, which lowers friction for very fast mortar removal.
Blades not lasting through the wall?
Mortar is abrasive and eats a light segment. These are sintered with a higher diamond count for longer blade life.
It is used with angle grinders. Sizes are 4 to 7 inch at a quarter inch wide, most with a 7/8 to 5/8 arbor. Match the width to your joint.
tiger-tuck-point: Need a standard tuck pointer to keep on hand?
The Tiger is our standard tuck point for mortar removal, grout repair and cleaning concrete joints. A plain value blade that cuts quick.
Either one. Tuck points are most commonly run on angle grinders, dry or wet.
The stocked blades are a quarter inch wide in 4 to 7 inch. Other thicknesses are available on request, so tell us your joint width.
single-row: Need a lot of material gone in a hurry?
Fewer segments means a more aggressive cut. The Single Row is very aggressive stock removal for when the high spot just has to go.
Will it leave a clean floor?
No. A single row will leave horseshoe marks on the material. If the finish matters, use a Double Row or a Turbo Cup.
Aggressive grinding builds heat fast. Cooling holes in the wheel help keep it from overheating. It comes in 4 and 7 inch, threaded 5/8-11 or with a 7/8 to 5/8 hole.
t-seg: Glue and epoxy smear and load up a tight wheel. The T-Seg has an open pattern of T-shaped segments that resists loading up while it tears through coatings.
High spots need an aggressive wheel. The T-segment profile is aggressive for coating removal and leveling uneven surfaces, and it still leaves a fairly smooth finish.
It comes in 4 and 7 inch, threaded 5/8-11 or with a 7/8 to 5/8 hole. Ask what grinder is running it and confirm the spindle.
turbo-cup-supreme: Too many passes to get the floor smooth?
The more segments a cup has, the smoother the result. The Turbo Cup Supreme has fan-blade segments around the core for a smooth finish in fewer passes.
Wheel running hot under a dust shroud?
A shroud holds heat around the wheel. The Turbo Cup has double the cooling holes in the core to keep the wheel cool.
Hard concrete is tough on a lower grade of diamond. This is the supreme-grade turbo cup, for longer life on hard concrete. It comes in 4 and 7 inch. Check the listing for threaded or plain hole.
zec-wheel: Mastic or glue gumming up a diamond wheel?
Sticky adhesive loads up diamond segments. The Zec wheel is a silicon carbide disc, suited to grinding concrete and masonry and taking adhesive off concrete.
No. It is a silicon carbide abrasive disc, so it wears down as you use it. It is an economy item for cleanup grinding.
It comes in 4.5 and 7 inch with a 7/8 to 5/8 arbor for angle grinders. Match the size to your grinder and guard.
arix-green-kut-green: Medium hard rock in your slabs?
Aggregate that runs on the hard side wears a softer-rock blade wrong. Green is the Arix bond matched to medium hard aggregate, so the blade cuts clean in that mix.
In an ordinary segment the diamonds land wherever they fall. Arix lines them up in an arranged pattern, so the segment cuts evenly from the first joint to the last one.
It depends on the joint spec and your saw. Arix Green runs 6 to 14 inch, with a wide quarter inch blade in a few sizes. Check the list before you order.
arix-green-kut-orange: Aggregate on the softer side of medium?
A blade bonded for hard rock does not wear right in softer stone. Orange is the Arix bond for medium soft aggregate, so it stays matched to your mix.
Joints not as crisp as they should be?
Clumped diamonds cut unevenly and rough up the edge. Arix places the diamonds in a set pattern, which gives a more precise cut and a cleaner finish on the joint.
Does it fit my early-entry saw?
Check the diameter and width your saw takes. Arix Orange is stocked from 6 to 14 inch. Put a good skid plate on with the new blade.
arix-green-kut-red: Most mixes are neither very soft nor very hard. Red is the Arix bond matched to medium aggregate, which makes it the common starting point when the rock is average.
Blade slowing down partway through its life?
Random diamond placement leaves weak spots in a segment. With Arix the diamonds are arranged so fresh ones keep coming to the surface in order, and the cut speed stays steadier.
Match your saw. Arix Red runs 6, 8, 10, 12, 13.5 and 14 inch, with some sizes in a quarter inch width for wider joints.
arix-green-kut-yellow: Soft aggregate chewing up your blades?
Soft aggregate is often abrasive and wears the wrong bond away early. Yellow is the Arix bond matched to soft aggregate, built to hold up in that mix.
Why pay attention to diamond placement?
Diamonds do the cutting. Arix sets them in an arranged pattern instead of a random mix, so more of them are working at once. That is the step up from the standard Green Kut.
What should I check before ordering?
Confirm the color for your rock, then the diameter and width for your saw. Arix Yellow is stocked from 6 to 14 inch. If you are unsure of the aggregate, ask your rep.
green-concrete-2-bond: Small early-entry saw and a green slab?
This is a 6 inch early-entry blade for green concrete, made with two bonds. It is a single-size item, so the details are short.
What should I check before ordering?
It is 6 inch by .095 wide. Confirm your early-entry saw takes a 6 inch blade and that the arbor pattern matches.
Not sure it suits your aggregate?
Early-entry blades are bonded to the rock in the mix. If you know your aggregate, the color-coded Green Kut blades let you match it. Ask your rep if you are unsure.
green-kut-black: Critically hard aggregate stopping your blade?
The hardest rock will glaze a blade bonded for anything softer. Black is the Green Kut bond for critically hard aggregate, the far end of the color range.
Need joints in the same day?
Wait too long and the slab picks its own crack. Green Kut is an early-entry blade for cutting control joints the same day, run dry on an early-entry saw.
Not sure the rock is that hard?
Black is for the extreme end. If Purple is cutting well, stay there. Tell us where the job is and what the aggregate is, and we will match the color.
green-kut-green: Aggregate on the hard side of medium?
Bond color follows the rock. Green is the Green Kut bond for medium hard aggregate, one step harder than Red and one under Purple.
A blade that is wrong for the mix drags and tears the edge. Matching the bond to the aggregate helps the blade cut freely, which helps the joint come out clean.
Dry cutting on a new slab?
Water and slurry are trouble on fresh flatwork. Green Kut runs dry on an early-entry saw. It is stocked from 6 to 14 inch.
green-kut-next-day: Could not get to the slab until the next morning?
Overnight the concrete gets a lot harder, and a same-day bond struggles in it. Next Day is a Green Kut bond made for slabs you cut the next day.
Harder concrete fights the blade and the edge can spall. This blade has laser-fused segments and is made to cut crisp joint channels in next-day concrete.
Blade heating on long dry runs?
Dry cutting harder concrete builds heat. Deep cooling gullets clear dust and help control heat. It comes in 6.5 and 13.5 inch, so check your saw.
green-kut-orange: Rock in the mix a little soft?
Orange is the Green Kut bond for medium soft aggregate. It sits between Yellow for soft rock and Red for medium.
Cut in the green zone with the wrong bond and the edge tears. With the color matched to your aggregate, the blade is made to cut the same day with less raveling.
What do I check when I reorder?
Color first, then diameter and width. Orange is stocked from 6 to 14 inch. It runs dry, and a fresh skid plate helps protect the joint edge.
green-kut-red: Not sure which color to start with?
Red is the Green Kut bond for medium aggregate, the middle of the range. If the blade wears too fast or cuts too slow, we move you a color either way.
Why does the color matter so much?
Aggregate is different from one region to the next. Each color is a different bond for a different rock, and the wrong one is the usual reason a blade disappoints.
Red has the widest size list in the Green Kut line, from 6 through 14 inch including 6.5. It runs dry on early-entry saws.
green-kut-yellow: Soft aggregate wearing blades out early?
Yellow is the Green Kut bond for soft aggregate, the soft end of the color range. Matching it to soft rock helps the blade last the way it should.
Cutting in the first hours after the pour?
The green zone is the window to place control joints before final set. Green Kut is an early-entry blade made for that window, so joints go in the same day.
Not needed. Green Kut runs dry, so there is no slurry to manage on new concrete. It is stocked from 6 to 14 inch.
skid-plates: Joints chipping even with a new blade?
The skid plate rides the slab right at the blade and holds the surface down. When the slot wears wide, the joint edge can start to chip. Check the plate at every blade change.
Plates are sized to the blade. They are listed for 6 to 8 inch, 10 inch, 13.5 inch and 14 inch blades. Order the plate that matches your blade diameter.
A wide blade needs a wider slot. There is a separate 13.5 inch plate for the .250 wide blade, so check blade width as well as diameter.
zenesis-green-kut-green: Medium hard aggregate wearing blades unevenly?
Rock on the harder side needs a bond made for it. Green is the Zenesis bond matched to medium hard aggregate, so the blade wears the way it was designed to.
Want more out of each early-entry blade?
Wasted diamonds are wasted blade. Zenesis diamond alignment places the diamonds evenly through the segment, which gives a combination of speed and blade life.
Random cracks beating you to the joint?
A slab needs its relief cuts early. The Zenesis Green Kut runs dry on an early-entry saw so you can cut right behind the finishers and leave a chip-free joint.
zenesis-green-kut-orange: Medium soft aggregate in your pours?
Softer rock calls for a different bond than hard rock. Orange is the Zenesis bond matched to medium soft aggregate.
Why is Zenesis the top early-entry blade we sell?
It comes down to where the diamonds sit. Zenesis arranges them in a pattern instead of a random mix, so the blade cuts fast, wears evenly and finishes clean.
Joint width is set by the spec. Zenesis comes in several thicknesses, and not every thickness comes in every size. Check diameter and width together.
zenesis-green-kut-red: Average aggregate, want the top blade?
Red is the Zenesis bond matched to medium aggregate. It is the color most crews try first when the rock is neither soft nor hard.
Rough joint edges on fresh slabs?
Uneven diamond spacing makes a blade grab and chip. Zenesis diamond alignment spaces the diamonds evenly, which is how it delivers chip-free cuts in green concrete.
Zenesis Green Kut is available in arbor patterns for the common early-entry saws, from 6 to 14 inch. Tell us the saw you run and we will confirm the fit.
zenesis-green-kut-yellow: Soft, sandy aggregate in the mix?
Soft aggregate tends to be abrasive, and the wrong bond wears away quick in it. Yellow is the Zenesis bond matched to soft aggregate.
Tired of trading speed for blade life?
Most early-entry blades give you one or the other. With the diamonds aligned through the segment, Zenesis is designed to give both, and it is the top of our early-entry line.
What should I have ready when I reorder?
Color, diameter, thickness and the saw. Zenesis Yellow runs from 6 to 14 inch in several widths. A new skid plate with the blade helps keep joints clean.
3mlb-low-hp-concrete: Blade glazing on your small walk-behind?
A bond made for a big saw stays closed on a small one, because low horsepower does not push hard enough to open it up. This blade is bonded for low-horsepower saws cutting cured concrete.
Is one wet blade right for every region?
No. Aggregate changes from state to state, so the bond has to suit the rock. This series is listed in several bond specs. Tell us where you cut and we will match it.
Thinner blades cut faster and thicker ones are more durable. Sizes run from 14 inch up, in several widths. These are wet blades, so run them with water.
americut-looping: Cutting slots for traffic loop wire?
Loop wire needs a wider slot than a standard blade leaves. Americut Looping blades are wide blades made for installing loop detectors at traffic lights and parking lots.
Stacking passes to widen a joint takes time. These blades cut the width in one pass, in concrete and in asphalt.
Order by the slot the spec calls for. Widths run from a quarter inch to a half inch, in 12, 14 and 18 inch diameters with a 1 inch arbor.
cut-n-break-blade-set: Need replacement blades for a cut-and-break saw?
This is the two-piece 9 inch blade set for cut-and-break saws. The saw runs two blades side by side, so they are sold as a set.
Can I replace just one blade?
Replace both together. The two blades should wear at the same rate so the saw cuts evenly.
What should I check before ordering?
Confirm your saw is the 9 inch cut-and-break style. A standard cut-off saw takes a different blade.
kmlb-low-hp-asphalt-green: Asphalt wearing the core on your walk-behind?
Asphalt and green concrete are abrasive and grind the steel under the segments. This series is bonded for abrasive material and has undercut protection to keep the core alive.
Right blade for a small saw?
A blade has to match the power class of the saw. This series is made for low-horsepower walk-behinds. Running a low-horsepower blade on a big saw can cause segment loss or core warp.
Blade life or speed of cut?
In asphalt you usually lean one way or the other. The series is listed in more than one bond spec. Tell us which matters more and what you cut, and we will pick the spec.
prestress-blade: Need blades for the prestress plant saw?
Prestress saws take large blades with their own arbors. These are 32 and 36 inch blades made for prestress and precast plant saws.
Which arbor does my saw take?
This is the main thing to check. The blades are listed by saw type with 2 inch, 60mm and 5-1/8 inch arbors. Order the one listed for your saw.
Check the blade diameter and the .250 width against your saw. If you are not sure, send us the saw model and we will match it.
ring-saw: Need a deep cut from a hand-held saw?
A ring saw cuts deeper than a cut-off saw of the same size because it has no center arbor. This is the 14 inch Americut ring saw blade for concrete, block and pipe.
Will it fit my ring saw?
It is designed to be compatible with ring saws in general, but drive setups differ. Note which saw you are running when you order.
Rollers come standard with each blade, so the wear parts get changed along with the blade.
split-segment-wall-saw-blade: Deep wall cuts are slow going with the wrong segment. The split segment design on these blades is made for high-speed cutting on a wall saw.
Going through wall saw blades too fast?
The split segment design is built for longer life along with the speed, which lowers what each cut takes out of the blade.
Stocked sizes are 26 and 30 inch in two widths. Larger sizes are available. Match diameter, width and arbor to your wall saw, and run it wet.
americut-ductile-premium: Rough ends on your pipe cuts?
A ragged cut is hard to couple. The Ductile Premium has an abrasive side coating that cleans the cut as it goes, leaving a clean, square end.
Abrasive wheels shrinking as you cut pipe?
An abrasive wheel wears smaller with every cut, so you lose depth. This is a diamond blade, so it stays full diameter and gives you full depth cut after cut.
Yes. It is designed for ductile iron pipe and also handles cast iron. It comes in 12, 14 and 16 inch with 1 inch and 20mm arbors.
blacksmyth-railcut: Steel rail needs a finer bite than pipe or rebar. The Railcut is the second blade in the Blacksmyth series, made for guardrail with finer diamond for faster cutting.
Does the finer diamond wear out sooner?
It is made to give that speed without giving up the life of the blade, the same idea as the original Blacksmyth.
It comes in small sizes for grinders and in 14 and 16 inch with a 1 inch arbor for cut-off saws. It handles guardrail, angle iron and rebar.
blacksmyth-supreme: Worried about losing a segment in the trench?
Segments are welded on, and a weld is one more thing to fail. The Blacksmyth Supreme is a one-piece, vacuum-brazed blade with no separate segments.
Pipe closes on the blade as you finish the cut. The Supreme has diamond side protection, which helps keep it from pinching.
Metal and concrete on the same job?
Utility work mixes materials. This blade cuts ductile iron, cast iron, angle iron, rebar and concrete, so one blade covers the trench. It comes in 14 and 16 inch for cut-off saws.
rescue: Demolition material grabs a thin blade. The Rescue blade uses quarter inch thick carbide chunks that cut fast and are designed to resist binding, which matters when time is short.
It is a carbide-tipped demolition blade for metal, roofing and building materials, wood, tree roots, tar, fire doors, plastic and rubber.
It comes in 12, 14 and 16 inch with a 1 inch arbor for cut-off saws. Match the diameter to your saw and guard.
tyrolit-basic: These are aluminum oxide abrasive wheels for ferrous metals: structural steel, angle iron and rebar. They are free cutting with a strong cut rate and good life.
They are triple reinforced for stability. An abrasive wheel still wears down as it cuts, so check the wheel and the saw guard before each use.
UNV means universal arbor, which fits 1 inch and 20mm. They come in 12, 14 and 16 inch at an eighth inch thick for cut-off saws.
tyrolit-premium: Cutting steel all day with abrasives?
These use a premium aluminum oxide grain for when you need more production on ferrous metals, structural steel, rebar and metal decking.
Yes, they are suited to rail cutting. There is also a listing for ductile and cast iron, so order the wheel that matches your material.
They come in 12 and 14 inch at an eighth inch thick, with 1 inch or 20mm arbors. Check your saw's arbor before you order.
blackcat: Asphalt wearing out your concrete bits?
Asphalt is soft and abrasive, and a bit bonded for concrete does not last in it. The Blackcat is made specifically for coring straight asphalt.
Bit gumming up in the hole?
Asphalt needs plenty of water at the segment to stay clean. The Blackcat barrel has water channels on the outside to deliver more water to the coring area.
It is stocked in 15 and 24 inch barrels with 1-1/4 inch thread. Tell us the hole size and depth. It is a wet bit, so run it with water.
core-bit-extensions-adaptors: Extensions add reach between the drill and the bit. They come in 6 and 12 inch lengths, in 1-1/4 inch and 5/8-11 thread. Match the thread to your bit.
Bit thread does not match the drill?
Thread adaptors convert between 1-1/4 inch 7 and 5/8-11 in either direction. Check which side is male and which is female before you order.
Drill with its own spindle connection?
Some core drills use their own connection instead of a standard thread. There are adaptors listed by drill model. Have the drill model handy when you order.
dustless-dry-core-bit: Vacuum not pulling the dust when you core dry?
Most dry bits have holes in the barrel, so the vacuum pulls air through the holes instead of dust from the cut. These have a solid barrel, so the vacuum pulls where it should.
Slurry is a mess inside a finished building. These bits are made to run dry with a vacuum system, which controls the dust at the hole.
Every size has a standard 9 inch barrel with 5/8-11 thread for hand-held core drills. Diameters run from 1 to 6 inch.
smash: Want one bit for whatever the job is?
Carrying a bit for every material adds up. The Smash is a versatile bit designed to drill concrete, block and asphalt.
Rough, abrasive material is hard on a fancy segment shape. The Smash uses a straight segment design to help it last in asphalt and other rough materials.
Most sizes are stocked in a 15 inch barrel with 1-1/4 inch thread, and one size also comes in 24 inch. Tell us the hole size and depth. Run it wet.
valkyrie: Coring too slow in reinforced concrete?
Slurry sitting on the cutting face slows a bit down. The Valkyrie's turbo-style slotted segments move slurry off the face, so it cuts very fast in concrete and reinforced concrete.
Grinding the same slurry over and over wears diamond for nothing. Clearing it more effectively is how the slotted design helps the bit last longer.
Will it run on my drill?
It is designed for a wide variety of drills. Stocked sizes have 18 inch barrels with 1-1/4 inch thread, in a wide range of diameters. Run it with water.
husqvarna-k6500-prime-chain-system: Which chain fits my high-frequency chain saw?
This page lists bars and chains for the high-frequency electric chain saw system. Order the chain by the same length as your bar: 12, 16 or 18 inch.
Bars wear along with chains. Both are listed here by length, so check the bar rails when you change the chain.
A worn drive sprocket chews up a new chain. The drive sprocket for this system is listed here too. Reorder by the exact part number.
husqvarna-k970-chain-saw-system: Which chain do I order for a 14 or 16 inch bar?
Chains are matched by bar length and link count. The 14 inch bar takes a 64 link chain and the 16 inch takes a 70 link chain.
Cutting ductile pipe with a chain saw?
Concrete chain and ductile chain are different. There is a ductile iron chain listed for each bar length. Order by the material you cut.
Need the saw or just the wear parts?
The powerhead is listed by itself and as a complete saw with bar, chain and sprocket. Guide bars and sprockets are listed separately for reorders.
ics-613-680-gas-chain-system: What fits my 14 inch gas chain saw?
This page covers the 14 inch bar and 64 link chain for this gas chain saw system. Check your saw model against the page title before you order.
The 64 link chain is listed in a standard bond and a soft bond. Which one suits you depends on the material. Tell us what you cut and we will point you to the right bond.
There is a separate 64 link ductile iron chain. A powerhead with no bar or chain is also listed, so read the description before you order.
ics-633-695gc-gas-chain-system: It matters. The 14 inch bar runs a 64 link chain and the 16 inch runs a 70 link chain. Order the chain that matches your bar.
Each bar length has a concrete chain and a ductile iron chain. They are not interchangeable in the cut, so order by material.
Guide bars for both lengths are on this page. Check the bar when you change the chain and reorder by part number.
ics-695f4-force-4-gas-system: Which chain fits this gas saw?
This system has its own chain and bars, in 12 and 16 inch. Parts from other chain systems do not interchange, so order from this page for this saw.
There is a separate ductile chain listed in 16 inch. Use the concrete chain for concrete and the ductile chain for pipe.
The powerhead is listed with no bar or chain. Add the bar and chain in the length you want. Reorder by exact part number.
ics-814-pro-hydraulic-chain: Which chain for the 13 inch hydraulic saw?
This page is the 13 inch, 50 link hydraulic chain. Confirm your bar is 13 inch and 50 link before you order.
The chain comes two ways, one bonded for life and one bonded for speed. Pick by what matters more on your work.
Not sure which bond suits your concrete?
The right pick depends on the aggregate and the steel in the wall. Tell us what you are cutting and where, and we will point you to one.
ics-823-853-hydraulic-chain-bars: Match the link count. The 15 inch bar is 66 link, the 19 inch is 78 link and the 24 inch is 94 link.
Bars for these hydraulic saws are listed in all three lengths. Check the rails for wear when you change chains.
What should I check before ordering?
Confirm the saw model, the bar length and the link count. Reorder by the exact part number on this page.
ics-890f4-force-4-hydraulic-system: Which bar length do I run?
This hydraulic system lists bars and chains in 10, 15, 20 and 25 inch. Order the chain in the same length as the bar.
A ductile chain is listed for each length alongside the concrete chain. Order by the material.
The powerhead is rated for 12 GPM and comes with a short or a long whip hose. Check your power pack's flow and pick the whip you need. The sprocket is listed too.
rgc-c120-force-4-hydraulic-system: Match length and link count: 10 inch is 50 link, 15 inch is 57, 20 inch is 67 and 25 inch is 79. Guide bars are listed in each length.
Each length comes in a standard bond and a soft bond. The wrong bond is the usual reason a chain disappoints, so tell us what you are cutting.
Will my power pack run it?
This system is listed for 12 GPM hydraulic flow. Confirm your power pack matches before ordering.
rgc-c150-hydraulic-system: Match the link count to the bar. The 15 inch is 76 link and the 20 inch is 88 link. A 30 inch setup is listed too.
Chains come in a standard bond and a soft bond. Bond is matched to the material, so tell us what you cut and how the last chain wore.
These chains are listed for 8 GPM hydraulic saws. Check your saw and power pack before you order.
rgc-mini-c50-hydraulic-system: Which chain fits the mini hydraulic saw?
Two lengths are listed: 13 inch at 50 link and 15 inch at 55 link. Match your bar.
Bars for the mini saw are listed in both lengths. Change the bar when the rails are worn.
Both lengths come in a standard and a soft bond chain, listed for 8 GPM. Tell us the material and we will help you pick the bond.
stihl-gs-461-rock-boss-system: Which chain fits my 14 inch gas chain saw?
This page covers the 14 inch guide bar and 64 link chains for this saw. Confirm your saw against the page title.
There is a soft bond concrete chain and a separate ductile iron chain, both 64 link. Order by what you cut.
Check the sprocket and the bar. A worn sprocket is hard on a new chain. Both are listed here, along with the complete saw with bar, chain and sprocket.
dr-schulze-core-drill-motors-stands-pack: Which motor and stand go together?
The combos are listed by size. The smaller motor is paired with the compact stand or the mid-size stand, and the large motor with the heavy roller stand.
What power do you have on site?
The motors are single phase, three speed, and listed by voltage. Confirm the voltage at your jobs before you order.
The mid-size professional stand is listed by itself here. Check the largest bit diameter you plan to run against the stand and motor rating.
dr-schulze-d160v-drill-stand: Need a core stand one person can carry?
This is an ultra lightweight, compact stand at about 22 pounds. It is rated for coring up to 6 inch diameter.
How does it hold to the slab?
It has an integrated vacuum base and a low-maintenance sliding guide. It also has a laser positioning guide to line up the hole.
Need to drill at an angle?
The column tilts for inclined drilling up to 45 degrees. Check that your drill motor fits the 60mm clamp.
dr-schulze-d350r-drill-stand: This stand is rated for coring up to 14 inch diameter. It has a roller guide system and a durable cast base.
It has transport wheels, so one person can roll it into place. A laser positioning guide helps line up the hole.
The motor mounts on a quick release plate. Confirm your motor fits the plate before ordering.
dr-schulze-dk-32: Need a motor for big holes?
This motor is for drilling from 3 inch up to 16 inch diameter, wet or dry.
No. It is for mounted use only, so it needs a stand rated for the bit sizes you plan to run.
What should I check before ordering?
Check the power available on site, the stand you will mount it on and the thread on your core bits.
gorilla-gs-100: What blade does this early-entry saw take?
It takes blades up to 8 inch on a 7/8 inch arbor, with a 2 inch maximum cutting depth. Order early-entry blades that match.
The saw has a dust box with a blade sight window and a 2 inch vacuum port. It needs a vacuum that moves at least 250 CFM.
One person on the saw crew?
It is light enough for one person to load and unload, and it has front and rear pointers for cut accuracy. It is made for same-day or next-day cutting.
grinders-circular-saws: Grinders are listed in 4.5, 7 and 9 inch. Match the grinder size to the blades and cup wheels you run.
A variable speed 4.5 inch grinder is listed alongside the standard one. Pick it if you need to slow the tool down for the work.
The 7-1/4 inch worm-drive style saw is listed here. Check the arbor on the tool against the arbor on your blades before you order.
hilti-gas-saws: Gas hand-held saws are listed in 14 and 16 inch. The bigger blade cuts deeper but the saw is heavier. Pick by the depth you need.
Order blades in the same diameter as the saw and check the arbor on your saw before you order.
A 9 inch battery saw is listed here too. It takes 9 inch blades, so do not order 14 inch blades for it.
husqvarna-10-5-battery-saw-blades: Standard blade does not fit your 10.5 inch battery saw?
That saw takes its own blade size. These are the 10.5 inch blades made for it.
There are two: a masonry blade for brick, block and concrete, and a rescue blade for mixed demolition material. Order by what you cut.
What should I check before ordering?
Confirm your battery saw is the 10.5 inch size. A 9 inch battery saw takes a different blade.
husqvarna-fs309: Small repair cuts and no room for a big saw?
This is a lightweight, compact gas floor saw for small repair jobs. It is easy to handle and fits in a small vehicle.
It is listed with a 14 inch blade. A blade has to match the power class of the saw, so tell us the saw when you order blades for it.
What should I check before ordering?
Check the depth of cut you need against a 14 inch blade, and whether you will cut wet or dry on your jobs.
husqvarna-fs400: Road repair cuts in concrete or asphalt?
This is an all-round gas push floor saw for small road repair jobs, with up to 7.5 inch cutting depth.
The handle adjusts for a comfortable working position, and the weight is balanced for stability while sawing.
It is listed with a 20 inch blade. A blade has to match the power class of the saw, so tell us the saw and the material when you order blades.
husqvarna-k-760-cut-n-break: Need a deep cut from one side?
This saw cuts as deep as 16 inch from one side. Two blades make a core in the cut, and you break the core off with the breaking tool and keep going.
A big round blade runs past the corner to reach depth. The cut-and-break method lets you cut deep without overcutting at the corners.
It is delivered with twin blades and a breaking tool. Replacement 9 inch blade sets are listed separately.
husqvarna-k-770: This all-round gas cutter is listed in 12 and 14 inch. Pick by the depth you need, then order blades in the same diameter.
This saw has a semi-automatic belt tension system, which helps power transfer and belt life.
Long straight cuts on road work?
It can be mounted on a walk-behind cart for straight cuts or cuts close to the curb. The cart is listed with the power cutters.
husqvarna-k4000-electric-saws: Cutting indoors where gas is out?
This page has the 14 inch electric wet hand-held saw. Electric is the usual pick where gas exhaust is a problem. It is a wet saw, so plan for water.
A vacuum dust reducer for the saw is listed here. It needs a vacuum connected to control dust.
The electric cut-and-break saw is also here. It takes the 9 inch two-blade set, not a 14 inch blade.
husqvarna-power-cutters-batteries: Battery saw dead before the cut is done?
Extra batteries and chargers are listed here, including a quick charger. Keep a spare battery on the truck.
This page has 14 and 16 inch gas cutters, 9 and 10.5 inch battery saws, and ring saws in gas and hydraulic. Read the description before ordering.
Match the blade diameter to the saw. The 10.5 inch battery saw and the ring saws take their own blades, listed separately.
makita-9-battery-saw: The 9 inch battery saw is listed as a complete kit and as a power head only. If you already own the batteries, the power head may be all you need.
A spare battery and a dual port rapid charger are listed here. Two batteries on rotation keeps a crew cutting.
It takes 9 inch blades. Check the arbor size on the saw before ordering blades for it.
stihl-cutquik-saws: Gas cut-off saws are listed in 12, 14 and 16 inch. A bigger blade cuts deeper, and the saw weighs more. Pick by the depth you need.
Walk-behind carts are listed by the saw models they fit. Order the cart that matches your saw.
A 9 inch battery saw, battery and charger are listed here. It takes 9 inch blades, which are a different size from the gas saws.
walk-behind-early-entry-saws: They do different jobs. The walk-behind is for cutting cured slabs and asphalt. Early-entry saws cut control joints in green concrete the same day.
The walk-behind listed here runs a 20 inch blade and is a low-horsepower saw. Order low-horsepower blades bonded for your material.
Which blades fit the early-entry saws?
Early-entry saws take their own blade sizes and arbor patterns. Check the saw's blade size and arbor, then match the blade color to your aggregate.
dustless-technologies-shrouds-vacs: Shrouds are listed by tool: 5 and 7 inch grinders, hand-held cut-off saws, worm-drive saws, reciprocating saws and core drills. Order by the tool and blade size.
A shroud only works with enough vacuum behind it. The wet and dry vacuum here is listed for saws 7 inch and under. Larger units are listed for bigger saws or more than one tool.
Check the hose size and length for your setup. Hoses, a Y-connector for two tools and pre-filter bags are listed here. A full bag or a clogged filter cuts suction.
